correctness.rationale: Using grounded resistance decomposition, the two-pin Schur precision and discrete Brownian bridge conditional variance give the exact full-state trace. Strict balancing of integer tails gives \(F_n(d;\kappa)\). For \(\kappa=c/n\) the normalization converges uniformly, and the \(J_c\) derivative has one zero: it decreases for \(r\le1/2\), increases for \(r\ge2/3\), and is strictly convex in between. Its implicit optimum has exactly one stationary gain, by eliminating c, located at \(r=1-1/\sqrt7\) and \(c=(7+4\sqrt7)/3\); the small-/large-c signs prove strict reentrance. Exhaustive rational 20-gap comparisons prove \(P_{21}\) gap \(12\to13\to12\) with positive runner-up gaps. Symbolic and exact finite matrix verifier ran successfully. Numerical scaling checks are illustrative, not proofs.

value.rationale: Noise-corrupted leaders on one-dimensional formations are a natural and established decentralized-sensing design question. This exact continuum classification exposes an unexpected nonmonotone separation law: maximum spacing at an intermediate finite scaled gain exceeds the infinitely strong pin limit, unlike a naive monotone-spread heuristic. A complete exact 21-node witness demonstrates observable finite behavior and an exact rational reduction supports reproducible placement design. The new contribution is not merely a matrix-inversion identity or an arbitrary small numerical observation.
